newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa JSE says reverting to old trading system.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa JSE says reverting to old trading system.

text.p: The Johannesburg Stock Exchange said on Wednesday it had reverted back to its original electronic trading system after persistent problems with a new system brought trade to a standstill in the past three days.
"The JSE has reverted to JET (Johannesburg Equities Trading system) 1," JSE president Roy Andersen told Reuters.
"We have given brokers 30 minutes to adjust their orders to sizes required by JET 1. As soon as that is done we will open the market," he said.
The new software, JET 2, loaded at he weekend, allows all shares to move in tick sizes of one cent irrespective of the value of the share.
On JET 1 tick movements varied according to the value of the share.

System problems this week resulted in trade being halted twice on Monday and the opening of the bourse delayed by an hour on Tuesday. On Wednesday only 27 minutes of trade took place as technicians battled with the system.
